1.pericope_label: The word of the LORD concerning the dearth
debates: When the drought occurred
Whether the little ones sent for water are children or servants
Why prayers are called the word of the Lord
outliers: Clarke doubts that any particular dearth is meant, holding the calamity a standing risk of the climate
themes: Judgment announced before the event so it cannot be mistaken for chance
Mourning for the trouble rather than for the sin
Figures multiplied to arouse a stupefied people
Grief expressed by covering the head

4.pericope_label: The ground is chapt; the hind forsaketh her young
debates: Whether the word rendered chapt means cracked or struck with terror
What creature the word rendered dragons denotes
Whether the high places are hill-tops or watercourses
outliers: Ellicott concedes that the vivid English rendering chapt has no basis in the Hebrew and derives from a translator he names
themes: Nature described as sharing the shame of its tillers
Instinct overridden by want
A drought severe enough to exhaust the most enduring animal
Repetition used to deepen the picture

7.pericope_label: Thou hope of Israel, why shouldest thou be as a stranger in the land
debates: Why the prophet includes himself in the confession
What the rare word rendered astonied means
Whether hope names the people’s disposition or God’s promise
outliers: Calvin denies that hope here describes anything in the people at all, since he holds hope among them extinct
themes: A private prayer published to rouse others
Covenant as the only ground of the plea
Daring images of God as absent or helpless
Faith recovering in the last clause of the prayer

10.pericope_label: Thus have they loved to wander; pray not for this people
debates: How far the prohibition of prayer extends
Whether the rejected fast and sacrifice were hypocritical
What the opening particle of the tenth verse refers back to
outliers: Ellicott declines to call the fast and sacrifice hypocritical, holding only that they came too late
themes: A people no longer called his own
Wandering loved rather than merely fallen into
Intercession itself forbidden
Worship offered after the time for it has passed

13.pericope_label: The prophets say, Ye shall not see the sword
debates: Whether being deceived by false prophets mitigates the people’s guilt
Whether the opening exclamation expresses grief or astonishment
What the four named forms of false prophecy are
outliers: Clarke answers the plea of deception by observing that the people accepted those prophets without proof of their mission
themes: A prophet pleading for people he is forbidden to pray for
A prophetic order degenerated into seekers of popularity
Assured peace preferred to a discipline that leads somewhere
Discrimination required of those who hear prophecy

15.pericope_label: By sword and famine shall those prophets be consumed
debates: Why those who were deceived share the deceivers’ punishment
Whether the last word of the sixteenth verse means wickedness or punishment
How the two verses should be joined
outliers: Calvin repunctuates the passage so that prophets and people form one subject, against the received division
themes: Deceivers perishing in the calamity they denied
Credulity treated as culpable rather than unfortunate
Itching ears as the opening falsehood needs
Complaint of severity forestalled

17.pericope_label: Let mine eyes run down with tears night and day
debates: Whether the direction to speak revokes the earlier ban on prayer
What the wandering of prophet and priest means
Whether the sword and famine words are nouns or participles
outliers: Clarke reports and rejects a reading that makes the wandering prophets pedlars trafficking in their own predictions
themes: Grief commanded as a public spectacle
A prophet told to say aloud what he already felt
Nowhere left that is not a place of death
Language that becomes the seed of a later book of laments

debates: Whether the prophet is disobeying the ban on prayer
Whom the plural of the confession speaks for
Why the fathers’ iniquity is confessed along with their own
outliers: Calvin holds the confession a form dictated for posterity rather than a report of what the people actually felt
themes: Intercession resumed against an explicit prohibition
Promise used as the argument of prayer
Confession standing for repentance and not replacing it
Inherited guilt confessed as aggravation rather than excuse

21.pericope_label: Are there any among the vanities of the Gentiles that can cause rain?
debates: What the throne of thy glory refers to
Whether a covenant already broken by one party still binds the other
Whether prayer that argues with God is proper
outliers: Clarke argues that the covenant was necessarily annulled by the people’s breach, where the others treat the appeal to it as valid
themes: A plea resting on God’s character rather than on any extenuation
Broken clauses as the form the agony takes
Rain claimed as the prerogative of one God alone
Expostulation defended as the language of piety
